```json
    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-cmp-corner-ratios",
        "exact_quote": "Consider a future unit timelike geodesic starting at a fixed point of the double-null wedge, and put $Y_i=e^{-\\kappa y_i}$. Its maximal remaining wedge track has finite proper duration, has an angular limit, and ends in a branch or corner. Each $|\\dot Y_i|$ is comparable above and below to its positive initial value, and its screen velocity is bounded on that fixed track. Moreover there is $\\delta_c(y_0^{\\mathrm{in}},y_1^{\\mathrm{in}})$, independent of the starting unit timelike tangent, with $\\delta_c\\to0$ as both initial coordinates tend to $+\\infty$, for which $$\\label{cmp:ratio-control}\n e^{-2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}\n \\leq\\frac{|\\dot Y_0|}{|\\dot Y_1|}\n \\leq e^{2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}.$$ If the track ends at the corner, then necessarily $$\\label{cmp:corner-necessary}\n e^{-2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}\n \\leq\\frac{Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}}{Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}}\n \\leq e^{2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}.$$ For a general fixed starting point the same conclusions hold with a finite, not necessarily small, logarithmic-variation constant.",
        "source_id": "PM-264.3"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-cmp-corner-ratios",
          "exact_quote": "Consider a future unit timelike geodesic starting at a fixed point of the double-null wedge, and put $Y_i=e^{-\\kappa y_i}$. Its maximal remaining wedge track has finite proper duration, has an angular limit, and ends in a branch or corner. Each $|\\dot Y_i|$ is comparable above and below to its positive initial value, and its screen velocity is bounded on that fixed track. Moreover there is $\\delta_c(y_0^{\\mathrm{in}},y_1^{\\mathrm{in}})$, independent of the starting unit timelike tangent, with $\\delta_c\\to0$ as both initial coordinates tend to $+\\infty$, for which $$\\label{cmp:ratio-control}\n e^{-2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}\n \\leq\\frac{|\\dot Y_0|}{|\\dot Y_1|}\n \\leq e^{2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}.$$ If the track ends at the corner, then necessarily $$\\label{cmp:corner-necessary}\n e^{-2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}\n \\leq\\frac{Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}}{Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}}\n \\leq e^{2\\delta_c}\n       \\frac{|\\dot Y_0^{\\mathrm{in}}|}{|\\dot Y_1^{\\mathrm{in}}|}.$$ For a general fixed starting point the same conclusions hold with a finite, not necessarily small, logarithmic-variation constant.",

        "anchor": "stmt-pk-triangular-comparison",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an integer $k\\ge0$ and $C_0>0$. For each $T\\ge1$, let $0<L_T\\le C_0(1+T)$ and let $E_0,\\ldots,E_k$ be nonnegative absolutely continuous functions on $[0,L_T]$. Suppose nonnegative integrable functions $r_T,b_T,S_0,\\ldots,S_k$ satisfy, almost everywhere, $$E_j'\\le r_TE_j+b_T\\sum_{\\ell<j}E_\\ell+S_j,\n \\qquad 0\\le j\\le k.$$ Put $R_T(t)=\\int_0^t r_T$, $B_T(t)=\\int_0^t b_T$, and $\\mathcal Q_k(B)=\\sum_{q=0}^k((k+1)B)^q/q!$. Then $$\\max_{j\\le k}E_j(t)\n \\le e^{R_T(t)}\\mathcal Q_k(B_T(t))\n \\left(\\max_{j\\le k}E_j(0)\n       +\\int_0^t e^{-R_T(s)}\\max_{j\\le k}S_j(s)\\,ds\\right).$$ In particular, if $B_T(L_T)\\le e^{o(T)}$, the polynomial factor is $e^{o(T)}$ for this fixed $k$. A bound $b_T(t)\\le e^{o(T)}$ uniform for $0\\le t\\le L_T$ implies this integrated bound because $L_T=O(T)$.",
        "source_id": "PM-264.3"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
```

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Weighted smooth data seminorms** ([source](#intro:seminorms)): For a pair of smooth symmetric covariant two-tensors, define $$\label{intro:seminorms} p_m(u,v)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left[ \sup_\Sigma\rho^{1+j}\|\nabla_*^j u\|_* +\sup_\Sigma\rho^{2+j}\|\nabla_*^j v\|_*\right], \qquad m=0,1,2,\ldots.$$
- **Vacuum initial data space** ([source](#intro:seminorms)): Let $\mathcal D\subset(h_*,K_*)+E$ consist of the smooth vacuum data $d=(h,K)$ with $h$ positive definite and complete, satisfying $$\label{intro:constraints} R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-\|K\|_h^2=0, \qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-\mathrm d(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=0.$$
- **Future extension** ([source](#stmt-intro-extension)): A $C^2$ future extension of $(M_d,g_d)$ is a connected time-oriented smooth four-manifold $\widetilde M$ with a nondegenerate $C^2$ Lorentzian metric $\widetilde g$, and a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding $\iota:M_d\longrightarrow\widetilde M$ onto a proper open subset, such that a future-directed timelike $C^1$ curve $c:[0,1]\longrightarrow\widetilde M$ satisfies $$c([0,1))\subset\iota(M_d),\qquad c(1)\in\partial\iota(M_d).$$
- **Parallel positive curvature diagnostic** ([source](#cat:Q)): Set $$\label{cat:Q} Q_d(w,\tau)=\|\operatorname{Riem}(g_d)\|_{k_{d,w}(\tau)}.$$
- **Closed duration and curvature test** ([source](#pm-h-13)): Choose a countable relatively compact open basis $\mathscr O$ of $T\Sigma$. For $O\in\mathscr O$ and an integer $N\geq1$, define $$\label{cat:test} A(O,N)=\left\{d\in\mathcal D: \begin{array}{ll} T_d(w)\leq N &\text{for every }w\in O,\\ Q_d(w,\tau)\leq N &\text{for every }w\in O, \ 0\leq\tau<T_d(w) \end{array}\right\}.$$
- **Separated null-ray conserved quantities** ([source](#pm-h-18)): Set $$\begin{gathered} E=-k(\partial_t)=-k(\partial_T),\qquad L_z=k(\partial_\varphi),\\ D=k_\theta^2+ \left(\frac{L_z}{\sin\theta} -\mathfrak a E\sin\theta\right)^2,\qquad P=(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)E-\mathfrak a L_z. \end{gathered} \label{geo:constants}$$
- **Subexponential growth convention** ([source](#pm-h-11)): A bound $e^{o(T)}$ means that for every $\sigma>0$ the quantity is at most $C_\sigma e^{\sigma T}$; the constant may depend on the smooth datum and on a fixed derivative order.
- **Causal radius-dependent average** ([source](#st:reduction)): For a zero-past function $f$ define its radius-dependent causal average by $$\label{st:averaging} f_s(t,x)=\int k_0(\sigma)f(t-\sigma d(x))\,d\sigma .$$
- **Retarded parameter feedback** ([source](#st:feedback)): The feedback is $$\label{st:feedback} \begin{split} c&=\ell_C^p h_{\mathrm{co}},\\ a&=F(\partial_t)(\chi_{\mathrm{st}}\ell h_{\mathrm{co}}), \qquad F=\operatorname{diag}(F_m I_4,F_v I_3),\\ F_m(\zeta)&=\frac{\sigma_0}{(1+\zeta)^P},\qquad F_v(\zeta)=\frac{2\sigma_0\zeta+\sigma_0^2}{(1+\zeta)^P}. \end{split}$$
- **Double-null interior gauge** ([source](#in:gauge)): Let $y_0,y_1$ be future-increasing optical functions and set $$\label{in:gauge} \begin{gathered} s=\frac{y_0+y_1}{2},\qquad x=\frac{y_1-y_0}{2},\qquad \mathcal S=\{s=0\},\qquad q=q_0e^{-2\kappa s},\\ g=-2a\,dy_0dy_1+ \gamma_{AB}(d\theta^A-b^A dy_0)(d\theta^B-b^Bdy_0), \qquad a=qA. \end{gathered}$$
- **Branch and corner runout regimes** ([source](#cmp:runout-types)): In the interior wedge we call the following limiting coordinate behaviors its two *branches* and its *corner*: $$\label{cmp:runout-types} \begin{array}{lll} \mathcal B_+:&y_0\longrightarrow y_0^*<\infty, &y_1\longrightarrow+\infty,\\ \mathcal B_-:&y_1\longrightarrow y_1^*<\infty, &y_0\longrightarrow+\infty,\\ \mathcal K^+:&y_0\longrightarrow+\infty, &y_1\longrightarrow+\infty. \end{array}$$
- **Exterior weighted correction norms** ([source](#pm-h-107)): For a nonnegative integer $m$ and a decay exponent $j$, put $$\\|v\\|_{H^m_j} =\\|v\\|_{H^m(B_2)} +\sup_{L\geq1} L^j \\|v(L\,\cdot)\\|_{H^m(\{1<\|y\|<2\})}. \label{pk:constraint-spaces}$$
- **Flat vacuum constraint linearization** ([source](#pm-h-107)): The Euclidean linearization of $\Phi$, denoted only in this subsection by $P$, is $$P(q,p)= \bigl(\partial_i\partial_jq_{ij}-\Delta q_{ii},\, \partial_jp_{ij}-\partial_i p_{jj}\bigr). \label{pk:constraint-P}$$

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-baire-topology** [claim](#stmt-cat-baire) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cat-baire): Weighted uniform completeness, openness of positivity, and local smooth closure of the vacuum constraints. -> A Baire data space whose neighborhoods contain finite-order seminorm balls.
- **step-closed-finite-tests** [claim](#stmt-cat-closed-tests) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cat-closed-tests): Preserve compact geodesic witnesses using local Cauchy, geodesic, and parallel-transport stability. -> Closed duration and curvature tests, with tidal contractions controlled by the parallel curvature norm.
- **step-regular-exit-and-category** [claim](#stmt-cat-regular-exit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cat-regular-exit): Use intrinsic compact diamonds in a causal homotopy, then ambient geodesic flow near an extension boundary; apply the countable test covering. -> Regular-exit covering and the finite-observation criterion for meagreness.
- **step-kerr-ray-geometry** [claim](#stmt-geo-slicing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geo-slicing): Bend stationary time and analyze the separated radial potential and homogeneous horizon frequency. -> Spacelike outflow slicing, radial escape alternatives, and a strict horizon source.
- **step-trapped-flow-and-elliptic-cone** [claim](#stmt-geo-normal-hyperbolicity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geo-normal-hyperbolicity): Construct normal defining functions, use smooth angular return dynamics for tangent growth, and compute the projected stationary symbol. -> Normal hyperbolicity, spatial projected ellipticity, and exclusion of extra zero-energy trapping.
- **step-calibrated-stationary-estimates** [claim](#stmt-st-stationary-estimates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-st-stationary-estimates): Combine local spectral input, conic gauge calibration, elliptic smallness, and normally hyperbolic propagation. -> Bounded-frequency, high-frequency, and nearby-parameter stationary estimates with the supported outgoing transpose graph.
- **step-stationary-mode-families** [claim](#stmt-st-families) / [proof](#proof-stmt-st-families): Preserve profile identities with smoothing corrections, integrate stationary metric directions, and remove leading adjoint tails by Green pairing. -> Exact stationary reference families, compact probes, and adjoint tails permitting mildly growing stationary pairings.
- **step-causal-target-and-local-vacuum** [claim](#stmt-st-local-evolution) / [proof](#proof-stmt-st-local-evolution): Use radius-dependent averages, stable retarded filters, a compensator, and a small negative-order normal-acceleration solve. -> Controlled target defects and smooth local retarded evolution with vacuum propagation.
- **step-augmented-retarded-tests** [claim](#stmt-st-retarded-tests) / [proof](#proof-stmt-st-retarded-tests): Prove full-rank zero-frequency coupling, invert the augmented transpose in separate frequency regimes, and identify causal tested operators. -> Compact and radiation test bounds uniform down to the physical frequency boundary.
- **step-compact-low-transfer** [claim](#stmt-co2-low-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-co2-low-transfer): Pair cutoff shell forcing with retarded transpose tests, exploit the Wronskian good-derivative structure, and remove auxiliary temporal smoothing. -> A radius-small compact negative-order norm.
- **step-frozen-energy-and-sliced-control** [claim](#stmt-co2-sliced) / [proof](#proof-stmt-co2-sliced): Build time-local first-jet energy using transverse uncertainty, then pair sliced equations with adjoint modes and subtract a conic elliptic correction. -> Frozen dissipation, radius-uniform acceleration coupling, and integrable static coefficient differences.
- **step-actual-principal-and-compact-high** [claim](#stmt-co2-compact-high) / [proof](#proof-stmt-co2-compact-high): Absorb the differential principal change by algebraic symmetrization, estimate nonlinear source placements, and recover mixed jets after shell and lower-order interpolation. -> The compact high estimate with radius-small linear far coupling.
- **step-far-structure-and-point-inputs** [claim](#stmt-far-structure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-far-structure): Expand the lab equation and differentiated gauge; derive spacelike anchors, radial point estimates, ordered null projections, and projected news transport. -> All geometric and pointwise inputs for the far multiplier and source arguments.
- **step-far-currents-and-source-budgets** [claim](#stmt-far-estimate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-far-estimate): Combine signed corrected outgoing currents with raw lab-time currents, ordered source placements, direct acceleration averaging, and finite hierarchy weights. -> The far estimate and a radius-uniform coefficient in the sliced acceleration pairing.
- **step-exterior-base-closure-and-smoothness** [claim](#stmt-far-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-far-closure): Choose the far starting radius, then compact matching radius and plateau, absorb the coupled inequalities, and apply higher-order energy induction after base continuation. -> Global smooth vacuum cylinder evolution on a common base neighborhood and subexponential higher bounds.
- **step-exact-interior-profiles-and-entry** [claim](#stmt-in-entry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-in-entry): Construct exact Hamilton–Jacobi optical profiles with a common rate, integrate moving phases, and apply mixed time-radial trace estimates. -> Summable low-order cylinder errors and subexponential higher entry jets.
- **step-interior-low-and-pure-jets** [claim](#stmt-in-low) / [proof](#proof-stmt-in-low): Close paired angular currents together with Hodge, damped trace, metric, torsion, and shift transports; differentiate cross equations to recover pure jets. -> Uniform low bounds, summable directional envelopes, and flank limits.
- **step-interior-higher-continuation-and-labels** [claim](#stmt-in-continuation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-in-continuation): Use high angular currents and longitudinal recovery on fixed diamonds for restarts; exhaust to a full wedge before applying directional tail damping on expanding regions. -> A full smooth product wedge with subexponential higher jets and valid exchanged optical labels.
- **step-comparison-cauchy-assembly** [claim](#stmt-cmp-development) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cmp-development): Apply finite bridge stability, identify overlapping vacuum solutions by ordinary wave-map uniqueness, and glue along matching faces with complete bridge Cauchy control. -> An open comparison development inside the full maximal development.
- **step-exterior-completeness-and-runout** [claim](#stmt-cmp-classification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cmp-classification): Combine redshift compact excursion estimates with integrable outer track deformation, then use monotonic optical coordinates in the wedge. -> Finite-lifetime geodesics cross the cylinder and first run out at a branch or corner.
- **step-select-noncorner-branch** [claim](#stmt-cmp-branch-seed) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cmp-branch-seed): Integrate null-momentum logarithmic variation, apply the necessary corner ratio condition, and change the reciprocal null velocity components within ambient flow tolerances. -> A branch seed in the original open family, still subject to its closed curvature bound.
- **step-normalized-packet-and-deep-comparison** [claim](#stmt-pk2-deep-proposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pk2-deep-proposition): Use branch blueshift, normalized coefficient limits, triangular transport and gauge hierarchies, and a common-rate mixed energy comparison. -> An exact deep vacuum solution with a large finite tidal contraction and convergent backward entry state, conditional on accurate entry jets.
- **step-return-rays-and-constrained-beams** [claim](#stmt-pk2-beam-proposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pk2-beam-proposition): Prove backward radial escape and subsegment flow bounds, propagate complex phase and gauge-compatible amplitude jets, and match by triangular Gaussian superposition. -> An exterior approximate perturbation supported in a distant initial shell with controlled matching and residual errors.
- **step-supported-constraint-inverse-and-fixed-point** [claim](#stmt-pk-constraint-nonlinear) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pk-constraint-linear-2): Combine Newton tails with annular moment-free divergence primitives, solve a weighted nonlinear contraction at a base order, and differentiate rotation and dilation conjugates for smoothness. -> Exact smooth exterior correction preserving a protected inner ball and allowing asymptotic charge changes.
- **step-exterior-transfer-and-parameter-margins** [claim](#stmt-pk2-exterior-proposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pk2-exterior-proposition): Rescale and correct the beam seed, use causal protection and ordinary wave-map comparison, then choose frequency and formal accuracy after all finite derivative buffers. -> Exact early agreement and accurate entry jets, together with convergence in the prescribed finite data seminorm.
- **step-whole-bridge-observation-attachment** [claim](#stmt-pk2-attachment-proposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pk2-attachment-proposition): Attach finite ordinary exterior and deep solutions to an unrestricted lower bridge development using past-preserved strict sublevels and matching collars. -> The observation and convergent seed lie in the full maximal development while the entire initial correction tail is retained.
- **step-category-conclusion** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pk2-attachment-proposition-3): Choose the tidal threshold above the closed-test curvature bound, realize the finite observation inside a prescribed neighborhood, and take the countable union of nowhere dense extendible pieces. -> Meagreness of future-extendible data in the common base neighborhood.

```json
          "anchor": "stmt-geo-horizon-source",
          "exact_quote": "The outer-horizon generators are a strict radial source for the null ray flow parameterized by increasing regular time $t$ on spatial cosphere directions.           "source_id": "PM-264.3"

          "exact_quote": "Under the simultaneous finite-slab budgets, for some $\\kappa>0$, $$\\label{co2:high-bound}\n \\mathsf K_R\\le C R^{-\\kappa}(\\mathsf F+\\mathsf K_R)\n       +C_{\\rm fix}\\bigl(e_{\\rm in}+\\mathsf N^{3/2}\n                                 +(e_{\\rm in}\\mathsf N)^{1/2}\\bigr).$$ The acceleration and sliced static bounds enter this estimate only as coefficient smallness and nonlinear errors, not as additional linear forcing terms.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-co2-actual-comparison",
          "exact_quote": "For each level $(U,s,A_i)$ in <a href=\"#co2:levels\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"co2:levels\">[co2:levels]</a>, let $d_M^{\\alpha\\beta}$ be the change from $\\bar g$ to $g$ of the differential order-two wave coefficient in stationary normalization.           "anchor": "stmt-pk2-observation",

          "exact_quote": "Fix an integer $s\\ge3$. There are constants $\\epsilon_s,C_s>0$ with the following property.           "exact_quote": "For any prescribed small $\\delta_3>0$, the localization parameters and far threshold can be chosen so that the exact ordinary wave-map solution exists on this finite exterior domain and its error from $g+h^B$, in the required fixed mixed norms, is bounded by $$C e^{\\delta_3T}\n       \\left(A_T\\lambda_p^{-M_1}+A_T^2\\lambda_p^{P_0}\\right).\n \\tag{E3}\\label{pk2:exterior-error}$$ It is exactly $g$ on the earlier needed compact-in-radius region up to $t_T-\\alpha'T$, where $\\alpha'>0$ can be prescribed sufficiently small.         {
```

## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-finite-triangular-propagator**: The strictly lower-triangular comparison matrix has a finite exponential expansion because it is nilpotent.
- **invariant-triangular-polynomial-majorant**: For a nonnegative integrated coupling, the polynomial majorant bounds the maximum absolute row sum of the finite propagator.
- **invariant-common-rate-comparison**: The differential comparison retains one common exponential growth factor; lower-order integrations contribute a finite polynomial factor.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-full-theorem-certification**: Treat successful finite matrix checks as certification of generic future inextendibility. -> The checks establish only finite algebra associated with an auxiliary comparison argument; they do not verify vacuum evolution, constraint correction, geodesic attachment, or the category argument.
- **anti-unsigned-coupling**: Use the positive triangular comparison with signed coupling coefficients without further justification. -> The positive comparison and its row-sum majorant rely on the nonnegative coefficient assumptions.
- **anti-unbounded-order-uniformity**: Read the polynomial contribution as a uniform subexponential estimate over increasing derivative orders. -> The polynomial degree depends on the fixed order, and the source explicitly restricts the subexponential consequence to that fixed order.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. The proof of the triangular comparison lemma constructs a finite nilpotent matrix exponential and an explicit polynomial majorant. This harness checks that auxiliary algebra using exact rational arithmetic. Its coverage does not extend to the continuous differential inequalities or to the main inextendibility theorem.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON object with integer k and rational string B.
# PRECONDITIONS: 0 <= k <= 8; B is a nonnegative rational number.
# OUTPUTS: Exact rational matrix exp(B*A) and polynomial majorant Q.
# TIME: Polynomial in matrix dimension; rational costs depend on bit length.
# SPACE: Quadratic in matrix dimension, excluding rational bit storage.
# ARITHMETIC: Exact SymPy rational arithmetic.
# FAILURE: Invalid input raises an exception and exits unsuccessfully.
import json
import sys
import sympy as sp

def main():
    obj = json.load(sys.stdin)
    k = obj['k']
    if type(k) is not int or not 0 <= k <= 8:
        raise ValueError('invalid order')
    raw = obj['B']
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        raise ValueError('rational string required')
    from fractions import Fraction
    b_fraction = Fraction(raw)
    if b_fraction < 0:
        raise ValueError('negative coupling')
    B = sp.Rational(b_fraction.numerator, b_fraction.denominator)
    n = k + 1
    A = sp.Matrix(n, n, lambda row, col: sp.Integer(1) if col < row else sp.Integer(0))
    power = sp.eye(n)
    propagator = sp.zeros(n)
    majorant = sp.Integer(0)
    for q in range(k + 1):
        propagator += (B ** q / sp.factorial(q)) * power
        majorant += ((k + 1) * B) ** q / sp.factorial(q)
        power = power * A
    print(json.dumps({'matrix': [[str(propagator[row, col]) for col in range(n)] for row in range(n)], 'Q': str(majorant)}, sort_keys=True))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-fixed-rotating-subextremal-center** (hypothesis): The result concerns a fixed rotating strictly subextremal Kerr center. Uniform thresholds through vanishing rotation or extremality are not supplied. Blocked use: ['Apply the result at extremality or vanishing rotation.', 'Use a neighborhood threshold uniformly across the full parameter range.']
- **limit-local-vacuum-data-class** (hypothesis): The genericity conclusion requires smooth complete vacuum data in the specified small weighted neighborhood of the complete Kerr bridge. Blocked use: ['Assert generic inextendibility for arbitrary large vacuum data.', 'Transfer the conclusion to matter-coupled initial data without another theorem.']
- **limit-extension-regularity** (formal_scope): The tidal obstruction addresses the stated future extension regularity. Weaker metric regularities require additional signed or averaged transport control and separate nonlinear amplitude estimates. Blocked use: ['Claim future inextendibility at weaker regularity from the tidal normalization alone.']
- **limit-category-is-not-individual-decision** (nonconstructive): Meagreness is a topological genericity statement and does not decide extendibility of a specified datum or provide a probability law on initial data. Blocked use: ['Certify an individual datum as inextendible solely from genericity.', 'Interpret the residual conclusion as an almost-sure assertion under an unspecified distribution.']
- **limit-smooth-topology-and-finite-order-approximation** (approximation): Higher seminorms must remain finite, while the perturbation construction establishes convergence at a prescribed finite order. A fixed frequency exponent is not asserted to give convergence at every order. Blocked use: ['Replace smooth membership by a finite derivative check.', 'Claim simultaneous convergence in all seminorms for the fixed packet construction.']
- **limit-closed-tests-require-full-seed-families** (formal_scope): The closed tests bound maximal duration and parallel curvature throughout an open family of seeds. A finite collection of bounded sampled measurements does not establish membership or the existence of an extension. Blocked use: ['Infer future extendibility from finitely many bounded curvature samples.', 'Replace the full seed-family and proper-time conditions by a sampled diagnostic.']
- **limit-conic-not-base-ellipticity** (formal_scope): The stationary ellipticity assertion holds on a spatial conic neighborhood containing the projected trap. It does not assert ellipticity throughout a spatial base neighborhood of trapping. Blocked use: ['Use a base-space elliptic estimate across all cotangent directions in the ergoregion.']
- **limit-transpose-conjugation-and-index** (formal_scope): The same-sign outgoing conjugation of the physical spatial transpose is distinct from the transpose of the outgoing conjugated primal operator. An index computation alone does not establish invertibility. Blocked use: ['Exchange the two outgoing transpose realizations.', 'Use index zero as an inverse without proving trivial kernel.']
- **limit-retarded-reduced-evolution-margins** (hypothesis): Continuation of the reduced evolution requires bounded base wave norms, small parameters, controlled acceleration and coordinate inverses, and positive spacelike and outflow margins. Vacuum evolution also requires the stated constraint and gauge initialization. Blocked use: ['Continue the reduced evolution after its stated continuation margins fail.', 'Treat arbitrary reduced initial wave data as vacuum data.', 'Assume metric finite propagation for compact spatially nonlocal gauge operations.']
- **limit-simultaneous-exterior-closure** (hypothesis): Compact, far, static and modulation estimates close together with an ordered choice of scales. The acceleration pairing needs a far coefficient independent of the far starting radius. Blocked use: ['Assume the far estimate already holds for a global solution when proving closure.', 'Replace the radius-uniform acceleration coupling by an uncontrolled radius-dependent coefficient.']
- **limit-higher-order-bounds-not-uniform** (formal_scope): Subexponential higher bounds are for each fixed derivative order and fixed smooth datum. Their constants may depend on the datum, order and prescribed region. Blocked use: ['Use the higher bounds uniformly over increasing derivative orders.', 'Infer a numerical growth constant for arbitrary supplied data.']
- **limit-interior-continuation-before-tail-estimates** (hypothesis): Finite-region higher estimates support continuation. Expanding-region subexponential estimates additionally require an existing full wedge with uniformly summed low bounds. Blocked use: ['Use full-wedge tail estimates to justify the prior existence of the full wedge.', 'Divide weighted curvature estimates by the degenerating lapse to claim uniform unweighted control.']
- **limit-comparison-region-and-first-runout** (formal_scope): The comparison region embeds into the full maximal development without being identified with all of it. Branch and corner runout describe limits of comparison coordinates rather than adjoined boundary points. Blocked use: ['Identify first runout from the comparison region with the maximal geodesic endpoint in the full development.', 'Claim that the comparison construction exhausts the full maximal development.']
- **limit-branch-selection-and-signal-hypotheses** (hypothesis): Branch selection starts with a regular exiting geodesic in an open seed family. The selected branch seed need not retain a regular ambient exit; the finite signal construction instead requires bounded parallel curvature on its branch track. Blocked use: ['Assume regular extension exit persists for the selected branch seed.', 'Invoke the finite tidal construction without its noncorner first-runout and bounded-curvature hypotheses.']
- **limit-packet-remains-approximate-before-correction** (approximation): The interior packet and exterior beam have controlled residuals. Exact vacuum data require the exterior constraint correction, exact gauge initialization and subsequent nonlinear comparisons. Blocked use: ['Treat a small beam residual as an exact vacuum solution.', 'Infer the finite tidal observation directly in the full development from the approximate packet.']
- **limit-deep-comparison-entry-and-strict-margins** (hypothesis): The deep comparison requires constrained wave-map entry jets, exact early agreement, the stated entry accuracy, sufficiently small packet norms and a strict error margin below the amplitude. Blocked use: ['Apply the deep comparison to merely approximate constraints.', 'Omit exact early agreement or the strict exponential comparison margins.']
- **limit-parameter-choice-order** (hypothesis): Finite derivative and trace buffers determine the positive frequency losses before the frequency exponent is chosen. Formal accuracy is chosen afterwards and the late observation parameter last. Blocked use: ['Increase formal accuracy while silently changing already fixed base loss exponents.', 'Demand a common frequency exponent for unbounded derivative orders.']
- **limit-protected-correction-tail-and-interior** (formal_scope): The nonlinear constraint solve requires a positive smooth symbol-bounded background and small stated base norms. It preserves the protected ball, permits a noncompact correction tail and changing charges, and asserts no constraints for the artificial interior. Blocked use: ['Require compact support or unchanged asymptotic charges from this correction theorem.', 'Assert the vacuum constraints for the artificial interior extension.', 'Remove the base smallness or positivity conditions.']
- **limit-whole-data-attachment** (formal_scope): The finite observation belongs to the full maximal development only after the Cauchy attachment retains the complete corrected bridge and its entire tail. Blocked use: ['Truncate the corrected initial tail at the computing boundary.', 'Promote an observation in an unattached coordinate patch to an observation in the full development.']
- **limit-finite-algebra-certificate** (formal_scope): Finite nilpotent matrix calculations verify only the auxiliary propagator algebra. They do not certify the continuous differential comparison, its asymptotic consequence or the vacuum inextendibility theorem. Blocked use: ['Use a finite matrix receipt as certification of the complete analytic argument.', 'Claim uniform asymptotic control when the comparison order increases.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every fixed rotating subextremal Kerr bridge, we prove that smooth vacuum data admitting a <i>C</i><sup>2</sup> future extension of their full maximal globally hyperbolic development form a meagre set in a neighborhood defined by one finite-order seminorm. The topology allows arbitrary symbol-bounded asymptotically flat tails and imposes no symmetry.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

Strong cosmic censorship asks whether generic initial data determine a spacetime that cannot be continued beyond its maximal globally hyperbolic development. The regularity of the proposed continuation is part of the question. Here we consider $C^2$ future extensions of vacuum developments near the complete two-ended bridge of an arbitrary fixed rotating subextremal Kerr black hole. No symmetry is imposed on the perturbation.

The exact Kerr development has a smooth Cauchy horizon. Nevertheless, we prove that data admitting any $C^2$ future extension are meagre in a weighted smooth neighborhood of its bridge data. The neighborhood requires smallness at only one finite order, and the allowed tails need not have prescribed leading coefficients. The conclusion concerns the full development, not just the portion covered by an exterior or double-null coordinate construction.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The precise statement

<a id="intro:seminorms"></a>
Fix $M>0$ and $0<\mathfrak a<M$. Let $(\Sigma,h_*,K_*)$, $\Sigma\simeq\mathbb R\times\mathbb S^2$, be the complete two-ended Kerr datum through the bifurcation sphere, with its chosen future orientation. Fix the connection $\nabla_*$ and tensor norm $|\cdot|_*$ of $h_*$, and a smooth $\rho\geq1$ agreeing with the Kerr radial coordinate outside a compact set on each end. For a pair of smooth symmetric covariant two-tensors, define $$\label{intro:seminorms}
 p_m(u,v)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left[
 \sup_\Sigma\rho^{1+j}|\nabla_*^j u|_*
 +\sup_\Sigma\rho^{2+j}|\nabla_*^j v|_*\right],
 \qquad m=0,1,2,\ldots.$$ Let $E$ be the space on which every $p_m$ is finite. Let $\mathcal D\subset(h_*,K_*)+E$ consist of the smooth vacuum data $d=(h,K)$ with $h$ positive definite and complete, satisfying <a id="intro:constraints"></a>$$\label{intro:constraints}
 R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-\mathrm d(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=0.$$ We give $\mathcal D$ the relative topology of all the seminorms <a href="#intro:seminorms" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:seminorms">[intro:seminorms]</a>. In particular, no leading coefficient in either asymptotic tail is fixed.

Write $(M_d,g_d)$ for the full maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of $d$, with the specified Cauchy embedding of $\Sigma$. We use smooth vacuum Cauchy theory and geometric uniqueness in the sense of (Fourès-Bruhat 1952; Choquet-Bruhat and Geroch 1969) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[ChoquetBruhat1952](#ref-ChoquetBruhat1952), [ChoquetBruhatGeroch1969](#ref-ChoquetBruhatGeroch1969)].

<a id="stmt-intro-extension"></a>
<div id="intro:extension" class="definition">

**Definition 1** (Future extension). A $C^2$ future extension of $(M_d,g_d)$ is a connected time-oriented smooth four-manifold $\widetilde M$ with a nondegenerate $C^2$ Lorentzian metric $\widetilde g$, and a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding $\iota:M_d\longrightarrow\widetilde M$ onto a proper open subset, such that a future-directed timelike $C^1$ curve $c:[0,1]\longrightarrow\widetilde M$ satisfies $$c([0,1))\subset\iota(M_d),\qquad
 c(1)\in\partial\iota(M_d).$$

</div>

We use signature $(-+++ )$. The extension need not be vacuum or globally hyperbolic outside the image. In particular, a regular geodesic exit is not assumed in this definition; it will follow locally from the extension and global hyperbolicity of the original development.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Local $C^2$ strong cosmic censorship). *For every fixed $M>0$ and $0<\mathfrak a<M$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that the data in $$\mathcal U_\epsilon
 =\{d\in\mathcal D:p_{10}(d-(h_*,K_*))<\epsilon\}$$ whose full maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum developments admit a $C^2$ future extension form a meagre subset of $\mathcal U_\epsilon$. Equivalently, the future-inextendible data contain a countable intersection of relatively open dense subsets of $\mathcal U_\epsilon$.*

</div>

Thus [thm:main](#thm:main) resolves positively the stated local $C^2$ strong cosmic censorship problem at every strictly subextremal rotating Kerr bridge. It is not a global assertion for all vacuum initial data, nor a claim at a lower extension regularity. Constants and $\epsilon$ may depend on the fixed center; no estimate uniform as $\mathfrak a\to0$ or $\mathfrak a\to M$ is claimed. Although all higher seminorms are finite, none beyond $p_{10}$ must be small.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### History and relation to earlier work

The Cauchy theory of Fourès-Bruhat and Choquet-Bruhat–Geroch (Fourès-Bruhat 1952; Choquet-Bruhat and Geroch 1969) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[ChoquetBruhat1952](#ref-ChoquetBruhat1952), [ChoquetBruhatGeroch1969](#ref-ChoquetBruhatGeroch1969)] makes the maximal globally hyperbolic development the natural spacetime determined by vacuum initial data. Sbierski (Sbierski 2016) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Sbierski2016](#ref-Sbierski2016)] gives a modern construction with explicit initial-surface and embedding hypotheses. The Kerr solutions (Kerr 1963) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Kerr1963](#ref-Kerr1963)] show why maximality in this class need not mean inextendibility as a Lorentzian manifold: their analytic continuation has inner Cauchy horizons, whose global geometry was analyzed by Carter (Carter 1968) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[Carter1968](#ref-Carter1968)]. Penrose’s cosmic-censorship programme began with the visibility of singularities in collapse (Penrose 2002) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Penrose1969](#ref-Penrose1969)]; his later strong formulation linked Cauchy-horizon instability to global predictability (Penrose 1979, sec. 12.3.2) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[Penrose1979](#ref-Penrose1979)]. The regularity of an extension and the topology used to define genericity are essential parts of a precise formulation.

The physical blueshift and mass-inflation analyses of Poisson–Israel and Ori (Poisson and Israel 1990; Ori 1991, 1992) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[PoissonIsrael1990](#ref-PoissonIsrael1990), [Ori1991](#ref-Ori1991), [Ori1992](#ref-Ori1992)] suggested that a Cauchy horizon can retain a continuous metric while developing a singularity in its derivatives. Dafermos (Dafermos 2003, 2005) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[Dafermos2003](#ref-Dafermos2003), [Dafermos2005](#ref-Dafermos2005)] established rigorous nonlinear stability and instability results for the spherically symmetric Einstein–Maxwell–scalar-field equations. In that model, Luk–Oh (Luk and Oh 2019a, 2019b) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[LukOh2019I](#ref-LukOh2019I), [LukOh2019II](#ref-LukOh2019II)] proved generic $C^2$ future inextendibility for admissible complete two-ended asymptotically flat data, combining exterior lower bounds with interior instability. Their data space and genericity topologies differ from those used here. For the vacuum equations without symmetry, Luk (Luk 2018) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Luk2018](#ref-Luk2018)] constructed weak null singularities, and Dafermos–Luk (Dafermos and Luk 2025) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[DafermosLuk2017](#ref-DafermosLuk2017)] proved continuous extendibility across a nontrivial Cauchy-horizon portion under quantitative assumptions on data already inside a black hole. This distinction between metric continuity and higher regularity is central to the present problem.

Recent results strengthen the vacuum interior instability picture. Gurriaran (Gurriaran 2026) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Gurriaran2026](#ref-Gurriaran2026)] proves curvature blow-up and locally Lipschitz inextendibility across a horizon portion near timelike infinity, assuming nonlinear Price-law asymptotics with a nonzero nonaxisymmetric leading curvature amplitude. Luk–Sbierski (Luk and Sbierski 2026) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[LukSbierski2026](#ref-LukSbierski2026)] prove formation of a continuously extendible but non-Lipschitz weak null singularity from characteristic data with quantitative decay and a weighted lower bound on a radiative curvature mode. Sbierski’s geometric criteria (Sbierski 2022, 2026) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Sbierski2022](#ref-Sbierski2022), [Sbierski2026](#ref-Sbierski2026)] explain how controlled parallel transport and robust signed curvature information obstruct Lipschitz extension. The Kerr interior instability results just cited concern a prescribed interior or horizon portion under explicit radiation hypotheses. The problem addressed here is to start with the complete weighted smooth bridge data and rule out every $C^2$ future exit generically. The finite perturbations below provide the needed curvature test violations without imposing a radiation lower bound on each starting datum.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### Exterior evolution.

The exterior estimates draw on both energy and stationary methods. The redshift estimate and the physical-space decay method of Dafermos–Rodnianski (Dafermos and Rodnianski 2009, 2010) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[DafermosRodnianski2009](#ref-DafermosRodnianski2009), [DafermosRodnianski2010](#ref-DafermosRodnianski2010)] were followed by boundedness, decay, and scattering for scalar waves throughout the subextremal Kerr range (Dafermos, Rodnianski, and Shlapentokh-Rothman 2016, 2018) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[DafermosRodnianskiShlapentokhRothman2016](#ref-DafermosRodnianskiShlapentokhRothman2016), [DafermosRodnianskiShlapentokhRothman2018](#ref-DafermosRodnianskiShlapentokhRothman2018)]. For radiative spin-two fields, the Teukolsky estimates of Dafermos–Holzegel–Rodnianski (Dafermos, Holzegel, and Rodnianski 2019) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[DafermosHolzegelRodnianski2019](#ref-DafermosHolzegelRodnianski2019)] and Shlapentokh-Rothman–Teixeira da Costa (Shlapentokh-Rothman and Teixeira da Costa 2023) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[ShlapentokhRothmanTeixeiraDaCosta2023](#ref-ShlapentokhRothmanTeixeiraDaCosta2023)] treat slowly rotating and full-subextremal Kerr, respectively. At the metric level, Häfner–Hintz–Vasy (Häfner, Hintz, and Vasy 2021, 2025) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[HafnerHintzVasy2021](#ref-HafnerHintzVasy2021), [HHV2025](#ref-HHV2025)] establish linear stability, using stationary spectral analysis and constraint damping; the full-subextremal mode analysis by Andersson–Häfner–Whiting (Andersson, Häfner, and Whiting 2026) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[AnderssonHafnerWhiting2026](#ref-AnderssonHafnerWhiting2026)] is an important ingredient. These linear results distinguish radiative decay from the stationary Kerr and gauge modes that must be tracked in a nonlinear argument.

Nonlinear stability for slowly rotating Kerr was established through the geometric and wave-equation analysis of Klainerman, Szeftel, Giorgi, and Shen; see (Klainerman and Szeftel 2021; Giorgi, Klainerman, and Szeftel 2022) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[KlainermanSzeftel2021](#ref-KlainermanSzeftel2021), [GiorgiKlainermanSzeftel2022](#ref-GiorgiKlainermanSzeftel2022)] and the constituent works cited there. Hintz (Hintz 2026) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[Hintz2026](#ref-Hintz2026)] establishes nonlinear exterior stability throughout the subextremal range for compact perturbations and a broader partially polyhomogeneous asymptotic class. That class has metric perturbations decaying like $r^{-1-\epsilon_0}$, with $\epsilon_0>0$, and a faster-decaying remainder; it does not directly include the arbitrary order-$r^{-1}$ symbol tails permitted here. We therefore prove the compact and far estimates for our data class together. Their wave-coordinate cancellation is related to the weak-null structure identified and used by Lindblad–Rodnianski (Lindblad and Rodnianski 2003, 2010) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[LindbladRodnianski2003](#ref-LindbladRodnianski2003), [LindbladRodnianski2010](#ref-LindbladRodnianski2010)]. The use of elliptic control at selected frequencies together with frequency-localized physical-space energy currents also has a close methodological parallel in the full-subextremal quasilinear-wave analysis of Dafermos–Holzegel–Rodnianski–Taylor (Dafermos et al. 2024) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[DafermosHolzegelRodnianskiTaylor2024](#ref-DafermosHolzegelRodnianskiTaylor2024)]. The tensorial gauge construction and its estimates are established here for the Einstein system.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### Exact data and finite signals.

Localized deformation of the constraints was developed by Corvino, Corvino–Schoen, and Chruściel–Delay (Corvino 2000; Corvino and Schoen 2006; Chruściel and Delay 2003) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[Corvino2000](#ref-Corvino2000), [CorvinoSchoen2006](#ref-CorvinoSchoen2006), [ChruscielDelay2003](#ref-ChruscielDelay2003)]; Carlotto–Schoen (Carlotto and Schoen 2016) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[CarlottoSchoen2016](#ref-CarlottoSchoen2016)] proved a further conical localization of asymptotically flat data. Our correction fixes an inner region while allowing an asymptotic tail, so it can change the charges. The explicit inverse uses a localized divergence primitive in the tradition of Bogovskii (Bogovskiı̆ 1980) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[Bogovskii1980](#ref-Bogovskii1980)], whose support and regularity properties are treated by Costabel–McIntosh (Costabel and McIntosh 2010) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[CostabelMcIntosh2010](#ref-CostabelMcIntosh2010)]. We prove the required inverse here because its support, derivative gain, and nonlinear dependence are needed in the finite experiment. Similarly, complex Gaussian beams and their superpositions provide the linear antecedents of the oscillatory construction (Ralston 1982; Tanushev 2008; Liu, Runborg, and Tanushev 2013) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[Ralston1982](#ref-Ralston1982), [Tanushev2008](#ref-Tanushev2008), [LiuRunborgTanushev2013](#ref-LiuRunborgTanushev2013)]. The matching of Einstein wave-gauge data and the bounds on time intervals growing with the experiment parameter are proved below.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
#### From regular exits to finite observations

The proof turns a possible extension into a finite condition that can be violated by a small vacuum perturbation. A $C^2$ extension supplies an open family of timelike geodesics whose proper durations and curvature components in parallel frames are bounded. A countable basis of initial geodesic states and integer bounds give countably many such tests. Each test is closed: a strict violation occurs on a compact geodesic segment and persists under a sufficiently small change of the data. Consequently, to prove meagreness, it suffices to violate the relevant test arbitrarily close to every datum admitting a regular exit. [sec:category](#sec:category) makes this reduction precise. Its decisive feature is that one large tidal measurement at a finite point suffices; the perturbation need not establish an asymptotic radiation law for the starting datum.

We obtain that measurement from the blueshift of a small oscillatory signal approaching an interior branch. In the optical coordinates used below, a branch means a limiting side where one coordinate remains finite and the other tends to infinity; at a corner both tend to infinity. These are coordinate-limit regimes of the comparison region. The main analytic work has two parts. First we construct a comparison development and control its geometry throughout one fixed neighborhood of Kerr data. Then, for a particular datum and a prescribed finite approximation order, we place a late signal in that geometry and realize it in the full development of nearby exact vacuum data. The distinction matters: the time and frequency of the experiment may depend on the chosen finite order, whereas the original $p_{10}$ neighborhood must serve all tests.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
###### Exterior control and the ergoregion.

The exterior construction combines stationary estimates in a bounded region with energy estimates on the asymptotically flat ends. Stationary time translation need not be timelike near all trapped rays at arbitrary spin. We instead separate directions in the cotangent bundle. [sec:geometry](#sec:geometry) constructs a horizon-crossing spacelike slicing for which the spatial projections of the trapped null covectors lie in a cone where the zero-temporal-frequency stationary symbol is elliptic. This directional ellipticity persists even when the base point lies in the ergoregion. [sec:stationary](#sec:stationary) uses the cone to localize the additional gauge terms and calibrate tensor transport while preserving the stationary modes and their time-translation chains. The stationary analysis of (Häfner, Hintz, and Vasy 2025) <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[HHV2025](#ref-HHV2025)] and the normally hyperbolic propagation estimates of (Dyatlov 2016; Hintz 2017) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[Dyatlov2016](#ref-Dyatlov2016), [Hintz2017](#ref-Hintz2017)] enter at the points specified there.

The compact estimate in [sec:compact](#sec:compact) couples the two-derivative elliptic gain on that cone to a one-derivative propagation estimate, with one additional source derivative, away from the projected trapped sets. On the ends, the weak-null cancellations and weighted energy currents control the arbitrary symbol-bounded tails in <a href="#intro:seminorms" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:seminorms">[intro:seminorms]</a>. closes these far estimates simultaneously with the compact estimates and the evolution of the Kerr parameters. The detailed far energy and source arguments are in [fe:section](#fe:section), [fs:section](#fs:section). All of these are estimates on an arbitrary finite interval of smooth existence, with bounds that permit continuation; a global nonlinear stability statement for this data class is not assumed. Once the low-order bounds close, each fixed higher derivative order has a subexponential bound with constants depending on the smooth datum.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
###### The interior and every possible exit.

[sec:interior](#sec:interior) prepares the data entering the black hole and constructs a double-null comparison region. Exact Kerr optical profiles, with their two ends normalized to a common positive inner rate, organize the lapse, angular metric, and transport equations. The low-order estimates control the geometry; the higher estimates control the finite derivatives needed later by the oscillatory construction. [sec:comparison](#sec:comparison) joins this region to the exterior and proves that the entire original bridge is Cauchy. Geometric uniqueness therefore embeds the resulting comparison development in the full maximal development of the same data.

We then follow the geodesic family supplied by a putative extension. Exterior completeness and the causal geometry force its relevant first exit from the comparison region to occur at an interior branch or in the corner regime. In the corner case, a small change of initial geodesic state within the same open family produces runout at a noncorner branch of the comparison region. Thus the original closed curvature test still applies to the selected geodesic. This step connects the local interior coordinates to an arbitrary future extension of the full development; it does not require the comparison region to exhaust that development.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
###### A small exact vacuum perturbation with a large tidal effect.

[sec:packet](#sec:packet) constructs a high-frequency signal near a late point of the selected branch. The branch geodesic measures an exponentially increasing optical frequency. Its contraction with the oscillatory curvature therefore yields a large tidal component even when the signal is very small at entry. A return-ray calculation and a complex Gaussian beam carry the required finite entry derivatives backwards to a distant initial annulus, with controlled losses. The subsequent forward comparison uses ordinary local wave-map reduction with the actual background metric as target.

An approximate signal does not yet give vacuum initial data. The exterior solve proved in [pk:constraints](#pk:constraints) and applied in [pk2:constraints](#pk2:constraints) supplies an exact correction that vanishes on a protected inner ball and retains a decaying tail at infinity. The tail allows the asymptotic charges to change and is included in the complete corrected bridge. A causal estimate shows that this correction cannot alter the earlier entry segment on which the comparison relies. Finally, the finite Cauchy attachment in [sec:packet](#sec:packet) places the tidal observation, its frame, and its geodesic back to the original initial surface in the full development of the corrected data. The resulting strict violation makes the corresponding extendible set nowhere dense. The countable union from [sec:category](#sec:category) completes the proof.

Figure <a href="#fig:proof" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:proof">1</a> displays the two constructions and the point at which they meet. The fixed background neighborhood is chosen before the test or approximation order. The finite derivative orders and their losses are chosen before the small frequency exponent; the formal accuracy and late time are then chosen to achieve the specified tolerance. In particular, the construction requires neither smallness of all higher seminorms nor one perturbation sequence converging in every seminorm at once.

<figure id="fig:proof">

<figcaption>The comparison region locates a possible regular exit. The separate finite experiment violates its closed curvature test in the full development of nearby data. Neither an exhaustive description of that development nor smallness at every derivative order is needed.</figcaption>
</figure>


The intermediate results also separate the evolution problem from the regularity of a proposed extension. The complete comparison development, the entry and normalized double-null estimates, the linear beam preparation, the exterior constraint inverse, and the whole-data attachment can be used when the final obstruction is holonomy rather than curvature. For $C^1$ extensions and for continuous extensions with locally square-integrable connection, one must additionally control signed or averaged parallel transport. Those uses require their own nonlinear amplitude estimates: the tidal normalization in this paper does not supply the larger-amplitude comparisons needed for these weaker regularities.

These regularity refinements are established in (OpenAI 2026a, Theorem 2.3) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[KerrCOne](#ref-KerrCOne)] and (OpenAI 2026b, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-34"></a>[[KerrWeakConnection](#ref-KerrWeakConnection)], respectively, as local residual statements near each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr bridge.

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
#### Scaling and conventions

It suffices to prove the theorem with $M=1$. Under the constant rescaling $g\mapsto M^{-2}g$, the induced covariant data become $(M^{-2}h,M^{-1}K)$. After identifying the bridge by dimensionless Kerr coordinates, this is a homeomorphism of the constraint spaces; the background connections agree and the tensor norms and radial weights change by fixed-order comparable factors. Completeness, vacuum maximality and the extension property are preserved. An original $p_{10}$ ball can therefore be chosen inside the inverse image of the rescaled neighborhood, and relative meagreness restricts to that open ball. We retain $M$ in geometric identities when doing so clarifies their dependence on the background.

We write $\mathfrak a$ for Kerr rotation when another local quantity is called $a$, notably a parameter derivative in exterior estimates or a null lapse coefficient in the interior. All spacetime and angular Sobolev norms are computed in the specified fixed charts or frames; on fixed supports, smooth changes give equivalent norms. Supported and extendible spaces at an outflow boundary are dual in the usual way. Symbol bounds on an end include all differentiated bounds, with an additional inverse radial power for each unscaled spatial derivative. A bound $e^{o(T)}$ means that for every $\sigma>0$ the quantity is at most $C_\sigma e^{\sigma T}$; the constant may depend on the smooth datum and on a fixed derivative order. These conventions will always be used at fixed subextremal parameters.

<a id="sec:category"></a>
### Closed tests and the finite-observation reduction

We first separate the topological argument from the evolution estimates. The facts in this section are independent of the Kerr parameters. We include their short proofs to make precise why a finite tidal observation suffices, and why no regular endpoint tangent is part of the extension hypothesis.

<a id="stmt-cat-baire"></a>
<div id="cat:baire" class="lemma">

**Lemma 1** (The data topology). *The space $\mathcal D$ is completely metrizable and $\mathcal U_\epsilon$ is Baire. Every neighborhood of a datum contains a ball $p_m(d'-d)<\eta$ relative to $\mathcal D$, for some finite $m$ and $\eta>0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cat-baire"><summary>Proof of stmt-cat-baire</summary>

*Proof.* A sequence Cauchy in every $p_m$ has compatible smooth limits on compact coordinate sets. Passing to the pointwise limit in its weighted uniform Cauchy bounds proves convergence to that limit in every $p_m$, including the finiteness of each limiting seminorm. Thus $E$ is a Fréchet space. For example its topology is defined by the complete metric $\sum_{m\geq0}2^{-m-1}\min\{1,p_m(d-d')\}$.

Any positive metric in the affine space is uniformly comparable to $h_*$: this follows from the decaying difference on the ends and compactness on their complement. Hence it is complete, and positivity is open already in the $p_0$ topology. The constraint equations are closed under local smooth convergence within this positive open set. An open subset of a completely metrizable space is completely metrizable, as is a relatively closed subset thereof. Consequently $\mathcal D$, and then its open subset $\mathcal U_\epsilon$, are completely metrizable and Baire. Finally the seminorms increase with $m$, so one sufficiently small ball in the largest of finitely many orders lies inside any basic neighborhood. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-13"></a>
#### Seeds and curvature measurements

<a id="cat:Q"></a>
A seed $w\in T\Sigma$ includes its base point. For datum $d=(h,K)$, its initial future unit velocity is $$U_d(w)=\sqrt{1+h(w,w)}\,n+w,$$ where $n$ is the future unit normal. Let $\gamma_{d,w}:[0,T_d(w))\to M_d$ be the maximal future geodesic with this initial velocity, parametrized by proper time. Along it parallel transport the positive inner product $1\oplus h$ on $\mathbb R n\oplus T\Sigma$, and call the result $k_{d,w}$. Set $$\label{cat:Q}
 Q_d(w,\tau)=|\operatorname{Riem}(g_d)|_{k_{d,w}(\tau)}.$$ The curvature tensor is covariant and the norm is its positive Hilbert–Schmidt norm, independently of any initial orthonormal frame.

Choose a countable relatively compact open basis $\mathscr O$ of $T\Sigma$. For $O\in\mathscr O$ and an integer $N\geq1$, define <a id="cat:test"></a>$$\label{cat:test}
 A(O,N)=\left\{d\in\mathcal D:
 \begin{array}{ll}
 T_d(w)\leq N &\text{for every }w\in O,\\
 Q_d(w,\tau)\leq N &\text{for every }w\in O,
                    \ 0\leq\tau<T_d(w)
 \end{array}\right\}.$$

<a id="stmt-cat-closed-tests"></a>
<div id="cat:closed-tests" class="lemma">

**Lemma 2** (Closed tests). *Each set $A(O,N)$ is closed in $\mathcal D$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cat-closed-tests"><summary>Proof of stmt-cat-closed-tests</summary>

*Proof.* Every strict failure has a compact witness. If $T_d(w)>N$, use a geodesic segment extending beyond $N$. If a curvature bound fails, use a segment through a point $\tau<T_d(w)$ with $Q_d(w,\tau)>N$. Smooth local Cauchy stability and geometric uniqueness place a neighborhood of this fixed compact segment in a common gauge for all sufficiently close data. For the compact segment $K$, its causal shadow $J^-(K)\cap\Sigma$ is compact; otherwise a limit of past causal curves to escaping initial points would contradict Cauchyness. Finite local Cauchy constructions therefore suffice. Geodesic and parallel-transport ODE stability preserve the strict witness. This proves openness of the complement, without asserting continuity of the maximal duration. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-cat-tidal"></a>
<div id="cat:tidal" class="lemma">

**Lemma 3** (Tidal contractions). *If $U=\dot\gamma_{d,w}$, $g_d(X,X)=1$, and $g_d(U,X)=0$, then <a id="cat:tidal-bound"></a>$$\label{cat:tidal-bound}
 |\operatorname{Riem}(U,X,U,X)|
 \leq (1+2h(w,w))^2 Q_d(w,\tau).$$ The factor is uniformly bounded for data and seeds near a fixed pair.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cat-tidal"><summary>Proof of stmt-cat-tidal</summary>

*Proof.* In the transported Lorentz orthonormal frame write $U=\alpha e_0+v$, $X=\beta e_0+z$. Orthogonality and the unit conditions give $\alpha^2=1+|v|^2$, $|z|^2=1+\beta^2$, and $\alpha\beta=v\cdot z$; hence $\beta^2\leq|v|^2$. Therefore $|X|_k^2\leq|U|_k^2=1+2h(w,w)$, the latter identity being constant by parallel transport. Tensor Cauchy–Schwarz proves the assertion. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-14"></a>
#### From an arbitrary extension to regular exits

We will use an intrinsic compactness fact. It avoids imposing causal convexity on the image in an extension.

<a id="stmt-cat-homotopy"></a>
<div id="cat:homotopy" class="lemma">

**Lemma 4** (Fixed-endpoint homotopy). *Let $P$ be a globally hyperbolic open subspacetime of a Hausdorff Lorentzian manifold. In a continuous family of future causal paths with fixed endpoints $p,q\in P$, if the first path lies in $P$, then all paths lie in $P$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cat-homotopy"><summary>Proof of stmt-cat-homotopy</summary>

*Proof.* Parametrize the family by a connected compact interval. The set of parameters for which the whole path lies in $P$ is open. Every such path lies in the intrinsic compact diamond $J_P^+(p)\cap J_P^-(q)$, which is closed in the ambient Hausdorff manifold. Continuity makes the parameter set closed as well. It is therefore the whole interval. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-cat-regular-exit"></a>
<div id="cat:regular-exit" class="proposition">

**Proposition 1** (Regular-exit covering). *If $d\in\mathcal U_\epsilon$ admits a $C^2$ future extension, there exist $O\in\mathscr O$ and $N\geq1$ such that $d\in A(O,N)$ and every seed in $O$ reaches its finite MGHD endpoint on a regular ambient geodesic arc. Here regular means that position and unit tangent continue to and through the endpoint.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cat-regular-exit"><summary>Proof of stmt-cat-regular-exit</summary>

*Proof.* Starting from [intro:extension](#intro:extension), identify the development with its image and write $z=c(1)$. The curve is future-inextendible within the development: an interior endpoint would equal $z$ by the Hausdorff property. Extend it maximally to the past inside the development. Cauchyness then puts a sufficiently late point $p=c(s_0)$ to the intrinsic future of $\Sigma$. In a small temporal chart at $z$, the local timelike relation from $p$ to $z$ gives a short timelike geodesic continuing past $z$. Only this local relation is needed, not a continuing unit tangent of $c$. For a $C^2$ metric the Christoffel symbols are $C^1$, so the geodesic flow has the usual local uniqueness and continuous dependence.

Consider sufficiently close geodesic arcs with starting positions on the same temporal slice inside the image, and close unit directions. They remain in a common compact chart and phase-space neighborhood. Parametrize these arcs by chart time on a common interval $[t_0,t_1]$, with the reference arc passing through $z$ at $t_z\in(t_0,t_1)$. Each nearby arc must exit the image. To see this, suppose an arc $(t,x_\gamma(t))$ stayed inside. Choose a fixed smooth bump $\beta$, supported in $(t_0,t_1)$, with $\beta(t_z)=1$. The paths $$\bigl(t,x_\gamma(t)+\lambda\beta(t)
                    (x(z)-x_\gamma(t_z))\bigr),\qquad 0\le\lambda\le1,$$ form a fixed-endpoint timelike homotopy: after shrinking the arc family, the spatial change is uniformly small in $C^1$, and all paths stay in the chart with its uniform timelike margin. Under the supposition that the original arc stayed inside, both endpoints belong to the image. [cat:homotopy](#cat:homotopy) would then keep every path inside, although the path at $\lambda=1$ passes through $z$, a contradiction. Thus every nearby arc has a first exit, with position and tangent regular there. By geodesic uniqueness this first exit is its maximal intrinsic endpoint, regardless of possible later reentry.

The reference arc continued backwards inside the development meets $\Sigma$. To see that a maximal timelike geodesic cannot end at an interior position limit, use a precompact temporal chart $(t,x)$. Causal slopes $V=(1,\mathrm dx/\mathrm dt)$ are bounded and the geodesic equation gives $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\log\frac{\mathrm dt}{\mathrm d\tau}
 =-\Gamma^0_{\alpha\beta}V^\alpha V^\beta.$$ Over a finite chart-time tail this bounds the unit tangent and gives its limit, so the geodesic continues. Cauchyness now gives the claimed intersection. Flow dependence through that fixed earlier compact segment yields an open seed family whose arcs have the exits just constructed.

Shrink the seed family to a relatively compact one. The earlier tube has uniformly bounded duration, parallel frames and curvature. In the extension chart, unit tangents stay in a fixed compact phase-space set. The parallel-transport ODE has bounded coefficients on a bounded chart-time interval, so its transport matrices and their inverses are bounded; curvature is continuous and bounded as well. Duration and the norm <a href="#cat:Q" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="cat:Q">[cat:Q]</a> are consequently uniformly bounded up to first exit. Choose a basis set $O$ within the seed family and an integer $N$ larger than both bounds. ◻

</details>

<a id="cat:cover"></a>
Let $B_\epsilon$ denote the extendible data in $\mathcal U_\epsilon$. Define $\mathcal B(O,N)$ to consist of the data in $B_\epsilon\cap A(O,N)$ for which at least one seed in $O$ has a regular exit in some extension. Then $$\label{cat:cover}
 B_\epsilon=\bigcup_{O\in\mathscr O,\,N\geq1}\mathcal B(O,N),
 \qquad
 \overline{\mathcal B(O,N)}^{\,\mathcal U_\epsilon}
 \subset A(O,N)\cap\mathcal U_\epsilon.$$ The pieces $\mathcal B(O,N)$ themselves need not be closed.

<a id="pm-h-15"></a>
#### The analytic task

<a id="stmt-cat-destruction"></a>
<div id="cat:destruction" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2** (Finite-observation criterion). *Suppose a single $\epsilon>0$ has the following property. For every $O\in\mathscr O$, $N\geq1$, $d\in\mathcal B(O,N)$, integer $m\geq10$ and $\eta>0$, there exist $d'\in\mathcal U_\epsilon$, $w'\in O$, and $0\leq\tau<T_{d'}(w')$ such that $$p_m(d'-d)<\eta,\qquad Q_{d'}(w',\tau)>N.$$ Then [thm:main](#thm:main) holds for this $\epsilon$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cat-destruction"><summary>Proof of stmt-cat-destruction</summary>

*Proof.* If the relative closure of $\mathcal B(O,N)$ had nonempty interior, that interior would meet the piece and, by <a href="#cat:cover" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="cat:cover">[cat:cover]</a>, be contained in $A(O,N)$. At an intersection point, choose a finite seminorm ball within the interior, increasing the order to at least ten if necessary. The asserted perturbation is in that ball but fails the test, a contradiction. Hence each closure is nowhere dense. The countable intersection of their relatively open dense complements contains no extendible datum, by <a href="#cat:cover" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="cat:cover">[cat:cover]</a>. ◻

</details>

All choices needed to fix the neighborhood in [cat:destruction](#cat:destruction) will precede the choice of $O,N,m,\eta$. The exterior and interior estimates construct the background comparison region at this common smallness threshold. Higher constants may then depend on the fixed smooth datum. Only afterwards do we choose the late finite perturbation that violates the selected test.

<a id="sec:geometry"></a>
### Kerr geometry and spatial microlocal separation

The exterior construction requires a spacelike stationary slicing, a description of all null rays that can remain in a bounded cylinder, and a spatial conic neighborhood of trapping on which the stationary operator is elliptic at zero frequency. We establish these properties for every fixed subextremal Kerr metric. Although the mass has been normalized to $M=1$ in the main argument, we retain $M$ in the identities below to display their parameter dependence. Throughout this section, $$M>0,\qquad 0<\mathfrak a<M$$ are fixed. Constants may depend on this pair; no assertion is uniform as $\mathfrak a\to0$ or $\mathfrak a\to M$.

<a id="pm-h-17"></a>
#### The stationary slicing and its ends

At either exterior end, let $T$ be the future Boyer–Lindquist time. In the trapped block we continue the corresponding sign of the Killing time, reversing the axial coordinate when necessary. Write <a id="geo:kerr-functions"></a>$$\begin{gathered}
 \Sigma_K=r^2+\mathfrak a^2\cos^2\theta,\qquad
 \Delta=r^2-2Mr+\mathfrak a^2=(r-r_+)(r-r_-),\\
 r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-\mathfrak a^2},\qquad
 r_*'=\frac{r^2+\mathfrak a^2}{\Delta},\qquad
 \kappa_\pm=\frac{r_+-r_-}{2(r_\pm^2+\mathfrak a^2)}.
 \end{gathered}
 \label{geo:kerr-functions}$$ In particular, $r_->0$ and both numbers $\kappa_\pm$ are positive; at the inner horizon we use the absolute value of the surface gravity.

The exterior computing cylinder will extend to an inner face $r=r_b$ with $r_-<r_b<r_+$. Its precise depth is chosen after the entry cylinder for the double-null argument and its finite margins have been fixed. The inner face is placed strictly deeper than that entry cylinder.

<a id="stmt-geo-slicing"></a>
<div id="geo:slicing" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5** (A bent spacelike time). *For any prescribed finite interval $[r_b,R_1]$, where $R_1>r_+$, one can choose a stationary time <a id="geo:time"></a>$$t=T+r_*-G(r)
 \label{geo:time}$$ with the following properties. One has $G'=1$ on the prescribed region, $1\leq G'\leq r_*'$ in a subsequent exterior interpolation, and $G=r_*$ near infinity. The function $t$ is regular at the future event horizon, its level hypersurfaces are spacelike, and $r=r_b$ is strictly future outflow. The delay $G-r_*$ at each fixed depth above $r_-$ can be made arbitrarily large by moving the exterior bend outward.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-geo-slicing"><summary>Proof of stmt-geo-slicing</summary>

<a id="geo:time-norm-one"></a>
*Proof.* Use the regular ingoing azimuth near the horizon, $$d\widetilde\varphi=d\varphi+\frac{\mathfrak a}{\Delta}\,dr,$$ and return smoothly to the Boyer–Lindquist azimuth toward infinity. These coordinates, together with $r$ and local sphere coordinates, give stationary spatial coordinates $y$; near infinity we use their Boyer–Lindquist Cartesian version. Let $b$ denote the Kerr metric in $(t,y)$. Direct substitution in the Boyer–Lindquist inverse metric gives <a id="geo:time-norm"></a>$$\Sigma_K b^{-1}(dt,dt)
 =-2(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)G'+\Delta(G')^2
      +\mathfrak a^2\sin^2\theta.
 \label{geo:time-norm}$$ For $G'=1$, the right-hand side is $$-\Sigma_K-2Mr<0.
 \label{geo:time-norm-one}$$ In the exterior it is a convex quadratic in $G'$. Its value at $G'=r_*'=(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)/\Delta$ is $$-\frac{(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)^2}{\Delta}
       +\mathfrak a^2\sin^2\theta<0.$$ Both endpoint values are negative, so every indicated interpolation is spacelike. Near the horizon, $t$ is the regular ingoing time minus the smooth function $G$. Between the horizons $b^{-1}(dr,dr)=\Delta/\Sigma_K<0$; with the chosen future orientation, $r$ decreases along future causal curves. This proves strict outflow at $r_b$.

Choose the additive constant of $G$ by imposing $G=r_*$ after the interpolation. Extending the interval where $G'=1$ changes the delay at any fixed smaller radius by the integral of $r_*'-1$ over the added interval. Since $$r_*'-1=\frac{2Mr}{\Delta}=\frac{2M}{r}+O(r^{-2}),$$ this integral tends to positive infinity as the bend moves outward. Thus the delay can satisfy all fixed-depth margins at once, while $G'=1$ continues to hold throughout the prescribed interval. ◻

</details>

As in [cmp:bent-time](#cmp:bent-time), the delays place the $t=0$ computing slices on or to the future of the bridge and separate their trapped-block portions by the required finite margins. The order of choices is important: first choose the entry depth and these margins, then choose $r_b$, and finally move the bend far enough outward. Lemma <a href="#geo:slicing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="geo:slicing">5</a> permits this order without altering the slicing on the prescribed interval. After proving compactness of the trapping radii below, we take $R_1$ larger than all of them.

Near infinity $t=T$, so all components and inverse components have the ordinary stationary Kerr symbol expansions. In particular, <a id="geo:end-expansions"></a>$$\begin{gathered}
 b-\eta=O(r^{-1}),\qquad b^{ti}=O(r^{-2}),\qquad
 \Gamma(b)=O(r^{-2}),\\
 r_*=r+2M\log r+O(1),\\
 b_{tt}=-1+\frac{2M}{r}+O(r^{-2}),\qquad
 b_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+\frac{2M y_i y_j}{r^3}+O(r^{-2}).
 \end{gathered}
 \label{geo:end-expansions}$$ Here $\eta$ is the Minkowski metric, and every remainder includes its differentiated symbol bounds. The terms of order $r^{-1}$ are rotation invariant. The leading term of $b_{ti}$ is a nonzero constant multiple of $(\mathbf J\times y)_i/r^3$, where $\mathbf J=M\boldsymbol{\mathfrak a}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak a}$ is the oriented spin vector in the chosen axes. These assertions follow by expanding the Boyer–Lindquist metric; the angular expressions and their rotations are smooth on the sphere.

<a id="pm-h-18"></a>
#### Radial dynamics and the horizon source

<a id="geo:separated-symbol"></a>
<a id="geo:ray-equations"></a>
We now classify the null rays in a large computing cylinder. A future null covector means a nonzero null covector $k$ whose metric dual $k^\sharp$ is future directed. Set <a id="geo:constants"></a>$$\begin{gathered}
 E=-k(\partial_t)=-k(\partial_T),\qquad
 L_z=k(\partial_\varphi),\\
 D=k_\theta^2+
     \left(\frac{L_z}{\sin\theta}
                    -\mathfrak a E\sin\theta\right)^2,\qquad
 P=(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)E-\mathfrak a L_z.
 \end{gathered}
 \label{geo:constants}$$ The angular expression is understood intrinsically at the poles: its expansion is the smooth round cotangent norm, minus $2\mathfrak a E L_z$, plus $\mathfrak a^2E^2\sin^2\theta$. The separated principal symbol in Boyer–Lindquist variables is $$q_E:=\Sigma_K b^{-1}(k,k)
       =\Delta k_r^2+D-\frac{P^2}{\Delta}.
 \label{geo:separated-symbol}$$ Stationarity, axial symmetry, and separation show that $E,L_z,D$ are constant along null rays. With a dot denoting the affine geodesic parameter, the corresponding equations are $$\begin{aligned}
 (\Sigma_K\dot r)^2&=P^2-\Delta D,\\
 \Sigma_K\dot T&=
  \frac{(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)P}{\Delta}
       +\mathfrak a(L_z-\mathfrak a E\sin^2\theta).
 \end{aligned}
 \label{geo:ray-equations}$$ These are Carter’s separated geodesic equations (Carter 1968) <a id="pm-cite-35"></a>[[Carter1968](#ref-Carter1968)], in the conventions used for the characteristic-flow calculation below.

<a id="stmt-geo-radial"></a>
<div id="geo:radial" class="lemma">

<a id="geo:double-root"></a>
**Lemma 6** (Radial alternatives). *For the fixed parameters above, future null rays in $r>r_+$ have $P>0$. If $E\leq0$, their allowed radial set has at most one simple turning point, and there is no photon trapping. If $E>0$, every trapped ray is a spherical photon ray, with constant radius satisfying $$F=\frac{2r\Delta}{r-M},\qquad
 \frac{D}{E^2}=\frac{4r^2\Delta}{(r-M)^2},\qquad
 F:=\frac PE=r^2+\mathfrak a^2-\mathfrak a\frac{L_z}{E}.
 \label{geo:double-root}$$ The energy-normalized trapped directions form a compact set separated from $r=r_+$ and from infinity. The relevant radial critical point is a unique nondegenerate minimum. A simple radial turning point reverses toward the same end of its allowed interval, and there is no homoclinic orbit from a double radial root back to that root.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-geo-radial"><summary>Proof of stmt-geo-radial</summary>

*Proof.* In the exterior, $$X=(r^2+\mathfrak a^2)\partial_T+\mathfrak a\partial_\varphi$$ is future timelike: direct evaluation gives $b(X,X)=-\Sigma_K\Delta$. Since $k(X)=-P$, pairing with the future null vector $k^\sharp$ gives $P>0$.

Suppose first that $E\leq0$. Then $P'=2rE\leq0$, while $\sqrt{\Delta D}$ is strictly increasing when $D>0$. The case $D=0$ cannot occur: it would force $k_\theta=0$ and $L_z=\mathfrak a E\sin^2\theta$, and hence $P=E\Sigma_K\leq0$. Thus the inequality $P^2\geq\Delta D$, on its positive-$P$ branch, has at most one boundary point, and that point is simple. It cannot contain either a double root or a bounded allowed island.

<a id="geo:radial-convexity"></a>
For $E>0$, restrict to the interval where $F>0$. Differentiation gives <a id="geo:radial-derivative"></a>$$\left(\frac{F}{\sqrt\Delta}\right)'
       =\frac{N}{\Delta^{3/2}},\qquad
 N=2r\Delta-(r-M)F,
 \label{geo:radial-derivative}$$ and $$N'=2\Delta+2r(r-M)-F,\qquad N''=6(r-M)>0.
 \label{geo:radial-convexity}$$ If $F(r_+)>0$, then $N(r_+)<0$. The strictly convex function $N$ tends to positive infinity and has exactly one zero beyond $r_+$; its derivative at that zero is strictly positive. Consequently $F/\sqrt\Delta$ has a unique nondegenerate minimum. If instead $F(r_+)\leq0$, let $r_0\geq r_+$ be its first zero. Since $F'=2r>0$, $$N(r_0)=2r_0\Delta(r_0)\geq0,\qquad
 N'(r_0)=2\Delta(r_0)+2r_0(r_0-M)>0.$$ Equation <a href="#geo:radial-convexity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo:radial-convexity">[geo:radial-convexity]</a> then gives $N>0$ wherever $F>0$. In this second case there is no radial critical point.

<a id="geo:impact-bound"></a>
A double root of $P^2-\Delta D$ must therefore occur at the unique minimum in the first case. Setting $N=0$ and $F^2=\Delta D/E^2$ gives <a href="#geo:double-root" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo:double-root">[geo:double-root]</a>. Moreover, $$\left|\frac{L_z}{E}\right|-\mathfrak a
                  \leq\frac{\sqrt D}{E}.
 \label{geo:impact-bound}$$ If double roots approached $r_+$, their identities would force $$\frac{L_z}{E}\longrightarrow
       \frac{r_+^2+\mathfrak a^2}{\mathfrak a}>\mathfrak a,
 \qquad \frac{D}{E^2}\longrightarrow0,$$ contrary to <a href="#geo:impact-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo:impact-bound">[geo:impact-bound]</a>. They cannot approach infinity either: <a href="#geo:double-root" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo:double-root">[geo:double-root]</a> makes $|L_z/E|$ quadratic in $r$ to leading order, whereas $\sqrt D/E$ is only linear. The radial range, the two impact quantities, and the normalized angular covectors are therefore bounded. Smoothness of the angular expression at the poles gives compactness in the intrinsic cotangent bundle.

Finally, the same one-minimum description classifies the allowed radial intervals. A simple endpoint is a reflection toward the same end of its interval. At a double root, $F^2/\Delta$ increases strictly in either radial direction away from the minimum, so a departing branch cannot turn back to it. There are no further radially bounded trajectories. Covector reversal gives the corresponding description of the past sheet. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-geo-horizon-source"></a>
<div id="geo:horizon-source" class="lemma">

<a id="geo:source-frequency"></a>
**Lemma 7** (The outer-horizon radial source). *The outer-horizon generators are a strict radial source for the null ray flow parameterized by increasing regular time $t$ on spatial cosphere directions.
