The mixed charge uses only the corrected $\xi_X$ cap in <a href="#fe:F12" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fe:F12">[fe:F12]</a>; it requires no $M$-weighted bound on an arbitrary uncorrected good derivative.

<a id="pm-h-102"></a>
#### Ordered derivatives and weight comparisons

For a target level $i$ and $|I|+j\le N_i$, write $\chi^i_{Ij}=Z^I(rT^jU_i)$ for the corresponding unknown of [fe:coordinates](#fe:coordinates). Positive sums over spatial-emitter words up to length $b$, with *fixed* lab-time count $j$, will be used; define lists, or sizes of lists, by $$\label{fs:lists}
\begin{aligned}
 V^U_{b j}&=|Z^{\le b}T^j U|,
 &G^U_{b j}&=V^U_{b+1,j},\\
 B^U_{b j}&=G^U_{b j}+r V^U_{b,j+1},
 &&\qquad U=h,\psi .
\end{aligned}$$ A superscript can equally be the level used. These letters with derivative indices do not denote the target or its velocity. In bulk $W_i^{1/2}G^i_{b j},\ w_{i,j}^{1/2}B^i_{b j}$ are controlled by <a href="#fe:F1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fe:F1">[fe:F1]</a> with spatial counts $\le b$. In uses of the time-slice cap, $B^i_{b j}$ is bounded by $C\sum_{|I|\le b}|B_1\chi_{I j}|$ plus $C V^i_{b j}$; we will charge the latter separately there. Similar statements hold for $G$ with $G_1$. These facts follow by commuting $Z$ at fixed $\partial_q$, using the first derivative formulas. Point entries on spheres, in $L^2_\omega$, include $$\label{fs:G1}
\begin{array}{ll}
 V^h_{b j}\lesssim N r^{-1+2\eta_*}\tau^{-A_H/2}&(b+j\le8),\\
 V^h_{b j}\lesssim N r^{-.48}&(b+j\le9),\\
 B^h_{b j},\ r V^\psi_{b j}\lesssim N w_H^{-1/2}&(b+j\le7),\\
 B^\psi_{b j}\lesssim N w_H^{-1/2}&(b+j\le6).
\end{array}$$ Use <a href="#fe:F7" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fe:F7">[fe:F7]</a>, <a href="#fe:F8" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fe:F8">[fe:F8]</a> (including expanding one more lab $T$ before the $Z$’s for the last bound). Two additional rotations give sup versions. In particular low $G^h$ has the bound of the first line, and low bad entries of either field have size $\lesssim N\sqrt{1+M}$.

<a id="fs:G2"></a>
Some comparisons used below, for large $r$, are $$\label{fs:G2}
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{W_i}{w_{k,j}}&\lesssim r^{p_i+.021}\tau^{A_i-A_k},
 &w_{i,j}&\lesssim W_i,\\
 \frac{w_{P,j}}{w_H}&\lesssim l^{A-A_H},
 &\frac{w_H}{w_{P,j}}&\lesssim l^{-(A-A_H)+7d_*},\\
 \frac{w_{0,j}}{w_H}&\lesssim r^{-.018}\mu^{-A_H}.
\end{aligned}$$ Write $m_{\rm cone}$ for the weight $m=(r^{-1}+l^{-1})^{-1}$ of [fe:section](#fe:section), to distinguish it from derivative counts denoted by $m$ below. For $i=0,P$, $\sqrt{w_{i,j}/w_{i,j'}}\lesssim m_{\rm cone}^{9d_*/2}$, and for $j'=j+1$ the bound is $C m_{\rm cone}^{-d_*/2}$. Indeed $q\ge-r$, $m_-m_+\asymp m_{\rm cone}$. On $|q|\le C r^\nu$ weights within each level are equivalent in $j$, and $w_{P,j}\asymp w_H$. Outside $|q|\le r^\nu$, $$w_H^{-1/2}\lesssim r^{(e-(\nu-\delta)A_H)/2}l^{-A_H/2}.$$ We use without further comment $r\widetilde a\lesssim N\tau^{-A/2}$, $|a(q)|\lesssim N\langle q\rangle^{-A/2}$ as coefficient bounds. When $|q|\gtrsim r^\theta$, $\theta=.45$, both $m_{\rm cone}^{-d_*/2}$ and $l^{(-(A-A_H)+7d_*)/2}$ gain more than $r^{-3\eta_*}$.

<a id="fs:G4"></a>
Two useful bad-commutation comparisons, with $c_0$ any bounded smooth coefficient of $n,s(q)$, are $$\label{fs:G3}
\begin{split}
 |\partial_q(c_0\partial_q\chi^i_{I j})| \lesssim&
 B^i_{b,j+1}+r^{-1}B^i_{b+1,j}+|a(q)|B^i_{b j},\qquad b=|I|,\\
 B^h_{b,j+1}\lesssim&
 B^\psi_{b j}+r^{-1}
             \sum_{i'\le j,\ b'+i'\le b+j+1} B^h_{b' i'} .
 \end{split}$$ Indeed $\partial_q(rT^j U)=krT^{j+1}U+s^d b_d Z T^j U$ and $Z$ commutes with $\partial_q$. For the second line express $$\label{fs:G4}
\begin{aligned}
T^{j+1} h=(1-s_s\cdot n)^{-1}
    \Bigl(&T^j\psi-r^{-1}s_s^d b_d Z T^j h\\
           &-\sum_{i'<j}c_{i'j}\,(T^{j-i'}s_s^d)
                                  \partial_d T^{i'}h\Bigr),
\end{aligned}$$ and likewise for $T^{j+2}h$, using the smoothing bounds. For example $Z^{\le b}s_s^d b_d ZT^{j+1}h$ from the latter identity after multiplication by $r$ costs $C r^{-1}B^h_{b+1,j}$ (here derivatives distribute on the expression). Extra $Z$’s on all bounded coefficients cost at most constants. Constants $c_{i'j}$ are combinatorial.

#### The complete source catalogue

**Proposition 34** (Complete far-source estimate). *For each commuted equation on such a finite slab, the sum of its budgets <a href="#fe:F14" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fe:F14">[fe:F14]</a>, together with its mixed charges <a href="#fs:mixed-charge" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fs:mixed-charge">[fs:mixed-charge]</a>, is bounded, for some fixed $c_1>0$, by $$\label{fs:F15}
 o_{R_0\to\infty}(1)(\mathsf F+\mathsf S_a)
 +C\sum_{\mathrm{prior}}\mathsf F_{\mathrm{prior}}
 +C(R_0)\mathsf K_R
 +C_{\mathrm{fix}}(e_{\mathrm{in}}+\mathsf N^{1+c_1}).$$ The finite prior order is: level $P$ before the two $h$ hierarchies; within each level lower total order first, then more laboratory times at equal total order, then fewer dilations $S$. Equal-index norms are aggregated. The constants on prior far quantities are independent of both matching radii. Small radial gains and nonlinear bootstrap products may cross this order. After fixed finite hierarchical weighting, [fe:energy-reduction](#fe:energy-reduction) therefore gives, for some $c_2>0$, $$\label{fs:F}
 \mathsf F\le o_{R_0\to\infty}(1)(\mathsf F+\mathsf S_a)
 +C(R_0)\mathsf K_R
 +C_{\mathrm{fix}}(e_{\mathrm{in}}+\mathsf N^{1+c_2}).$$ The initial and starting-annulus correction costs satisfy the same bound. In particular the pure acceleration defect on the starting annulus has its direct small radial coefficient on $\mathsf S_a$.*
